title: Checkpoint: Cinema Around the World
objective: After this level you can compare how Italy, France, Japan, India, Hong Kong and Nigeria each shaped cinema, and trace their influence on each other.
summary: Go-betweens and festivals carried this chapter's films abroad: Stramigioli sent Rashomon to Venice, and Open City shared the top prize at the first Cannes. The chapter maps six national cinemas.

cards.headline: Chapter 7 finale: films don't cross borders on their own.
cards.body: Every film in this chapter traveled far from home, and someone had to carry it. Here is who did, plus the chapter's whole map of world cinema in one breath.

events.label: Rossellini's Open City, shot in Rome's rubble
Kurosawa's Rashomon wins Venice's Golden Lion
Ray's Pather Panchali wins a major award at Cannes
Truffaut's The 400 Blows wins best direction at Cannes
Enter the Dragon joins Hong Kong and U.S. producers
Nigeria's Living in Bondage goes straight to VHS

cards.headline: The go-betweens
cards.body: An Italian carried a Japanese film to the world. Giuliana Stramigioli, president of the company Italifilm, recommended Rashomon to the selection committee in Venice, and it won the Golden Lion in 1951. Italy's own postwar cinema had gone the same way: Open City shared the Grand Prix, the top prize, at the first Cannes festival in 1946. Festivals, and the people who fill them, are cinema's border crossings.

cards.headline: The whole chapter in one breath
cards.body: Neorealists filmed ordinary people on real streets; Ray saw Bicycle Thieves and took that spirit to a Bengal village. Critics of the French New Wave rebelled against the polished 'tradition of quality'. Rashomon split one crime into four accounts, and Ozu kept his camera low and still. Hindi films inherited song from Parsi theatre; Hong Kong turned Peking opera training into screen fights; Nigeria built an industry on videotape.

cards.headline: Chapter 7 complete
learned: How Italy, France, Japan, India, Hong Kong and Nigeria each made cinema their own.
Why postwar filmmakers took cameras into real streets, and how that spread from Rome to Bengal.
Why Hindi films sing, and how playback singers lend their voices to the stars.
What festivals and go-betweens do to carry a film across borders.

questions.prompt: Who recommended Rashomon to the Venice Film Festival?

options.label: Kurosawa Akira, the director himself
options.rationale: The level credits an Italian go-between.

options.label: Giuliana Stramigioli of Italifilm
Philippe Erlanger of Cannes
Satyajit Ray
options.rationale: Ray was an Indian director, not a festival go-between.

questions.explanation: Italifilm president Giuliana Stramigioli recommended Rashomon to the Venice selection committee.

questions.prompt: From Level 64: what are Ozu's 'pillow shots'?

options.label: Close-ups of actors resting their heads
options.rationale: They show places and objects, not sleepers.

options.label: Short, still views of places placed between scenes
Handheld shots that follow a character around
Slow dissolves that blend two scenes together

questions.explanation: Pillow shots are short, place-setting shots of seas, boats, train tracks or rooms between scenes.

questions.prompt: How did Italian neorealism reach Indian cinema?

options.label: Italian studios opened branches in Bombay to make Hindi films
options.rationale: The link was a film, not a studio.

options.label: Ray saw Bicycle Thieves and set out to film on location with non-professionals
De Sica traveled to Bengal and directed Pather Panchali himself
Cannes required Indian entries to copy the style of Italian films

questions.explanation: Bicycle Thieves, shot on location with non-professionals, showed Ray that his own film could be made the same way.

questions.prompt: From Level 67: what training did Jackie Chan and Yuen Woo-ping both come from?

options.label: Peking opera
Film school in Paris
options.rationale: Their training was in opera, not film school.

options.label: Western boxing gyms
Hollywood stunt schools
options.rationale: They learned in Hong Kong opera traditions.

questions.explanation: Chan trained at a Peking opera school, and Yuen grew up in a family of Peking Opera performers.

questions.prompt: Festivals and go-betweens carry films across borders. Which Level 6 practice did that job in cinema's first years?

options.label: Kinetoscope parlors in New York
options.rationale: Parlors kept films in one place for one viewer at a time.

options.label: Paper prints sent to the Library of Congress
options.rationale: Those protected copyright; they did not spread films abroad.

options.label: The Lumières sending camera operators to cities worldwide
Méliès's glass studio near Paris
options.rationale: A studio makes films; it does not carry them abroad.

questions.explanation: From 1896 the Lumières sent trained operators around the world to show films and shoot new ones.
